harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired and deployed the UDP collector on node1. It now validates nonnegative decimal sequence/readings, appends valid records, persists duplicate detection across restarts, logs malformed datagrams separately, and starts automatically. The original `west,1,42` reading was preserved. Both nodes were rebooted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Created a root-only rollback copy at /var/backups/udp-meter-ingestion/collector.py.pre-repair.
Ran the collector as a restricted `udp-meter` system user under hardened systemd settings.
Allowed UDP/9098 through firewalld only from node2.
Verified end-to-end ingestion from node2, duplicate suppression, malformed isolation, and continued operation.
Verified collector-process restart persistence and duplicate-state reload.
Rebooted node1 and node2 one at a time, confirming changed boot IDs and recovery.
Confirmed RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Valid datagrams append; duplicate meter/sequence pairs are ignored; malformed datagrams are recorded separately without terminating collection
evidence.summary: Node2 sent malformed, valid, duplicate, and post-malformed valid datagrams. Node1 recorded valid pairs exactly once, isolated malformed input, and remained active/listening.

evidence.requirement: Previously recorded reading is preserved across collector restarts
evidence.summary: The original `west,1,42` was captured before changes. A collector restart changed PID without changing data checksums, and duplicates sent afterward did not replace or append existing keys.

evidence.requirement: Collector runs reliably and automatically with scoped network access
evidence.summary: The service is enabled and active under the dedicated account, listens on UDP/9098, and firewalld permits only node2's address.
Healthy baseline boot ID `19062a82…`, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID `f344d117…`, and recovered collector, firewall, listener, data, checksums, and zero failed units.
Healthy baseline boot ID `646e5f74…`, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID `8beeb0ba…`, restored network/firewall/data checksums, zero failed units, and successful post-reboot UDP transmission.

evidence.requirement: End-to-end behavior and data remain healthy after both node restarts
evidence.summary: Post-reboot traffic from node2 reached node1; malformed input was logged separately, duplicate input left readings unchanged, the protected reading remained exactly once, and the service stayed healthy.
